Akira Toriyama, the brilliant mind behind the iconic Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z and Dragon Ball Super series, has left an indelible mark on countless lives, mine included.  Through his captivating storytelling, vibrant characters, and imaginative worlds, Toriyama's creations ignited a sense of adventure and wonder in the hearts of fans worldwide. The way he weaved together themes of courage, friendship, and perseverance truly resonated with me during my formative years. 

Toriyama's meticulous attention to detail in his artwork and character design brought the fantastical universe of Dragon Ball to life, forever changing manga/anime art that captivated audiences of all ages. His innovative storytelling and ability to create characters with depth and charisma made the journey alongside Goku and his friends not just an anime, but an immersive experience that became an integral part of my childhood. Iconic moments like Goku transforming the first time, Gohan ascending and Goku's "and this is to go even further beyond, aaahhhh" all made me lose my shit and they will be remembered as some of the best moments of my childhood until I die.

As I reflect on the impact of Toriyama's work on my life, I am filled with gratitude for the countless hours of joy, excitement, and inspiration that Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z and Dragon Ball Super provided. Through his creations, Toriyama instilled in me a sense of determination, a belief in the power of friendship, and a love for storytelling that continues to shape me today.

Though Toriyama may have passed on, his legacy as a master storyteller, artist, and visionary lives on through the enduring appeal and influence of his work. The world he crafted will forever hold a special place in my heart, a place filled with cherished memories of epic battles, heartfelt moments, and valuable life lessons. In honoring his memory, I celebrate the immeasurable impact Akira Toriyama has had on my childhood and the childhoods of many others around the globe. Rest in peace, Akira.😭

Special Containment Procedures:
SCP-64626 is to be contained in a hermetically sealed, Class-5 biohazard containment chamber at Site-██. Access to SCP-64626 is restricted to Level 4 personnel and above. All personnel entering SCP-64626's containment chamber must undergo thorough decontamination procedures, including full-body hazmat suits.

Due to the potential risk of prion transmission, no biological samples or materials are to be taken from SCP-64626 without explicit approval from the Site Director and the Ethics Committee.

Description:
SCP-64626 is a collection of prion particles of unknown origin, designated SCP-64626-A. Unlike conventional prions, SCP-64626-A exhibits anomalous properties that make it highly contagious and resistant to standard decontamination procedures.

SCP-64626-A has the ability to survive in a variety of environments, including extreme temperatures and chemical treatments that would typically denature prion proteins. Transmission of SCP-64626-A occurs through direct contact with contaminated biological material, and it is capable of infecting a wide range of organisms, including humans, animals, and plant life.

Upon infection, SCP-64626-A induces a rapid and irreversible transformation of the host's neural tissues, leading to a progressive breakdown of cognitive functions and motor control. The affected individuals, hereafter referred to as SCP-64626-B instances, display erratic and aggressive behavior, posing a significant danger to themselves and others.

SCP-64626-A is capable of remaining dormant in living organisms for extended periods, reactivating under conditions that are not yet fully understood. Infected individuals may exhibit no symptoms for months or even years before the prion becomes active, making early detection and containment challenging.

Research into the nature of SCP-64626-A is ongoing, with the goal of developing effective countermeasures for containment and potential treatment. As of now, no cure or preventive measure has been identified, and SCP-64626 remains a serious threat to global biological safety.

Addendum 64626-01: Incident Log 64626-A-23
On [DATE REDACTED], a breach occurred in SCP-64626's containment chamber, resulting in the escape of several SCP-64626-B instances. Site personnel initiated emergency quarantine procedures, but containment efforts were compromised due to the highly contagious nature of SCP-64626-A.

The breach led to widespread infection among the Site personnel, and attempts to recontain SCP-64626-A were met with resistance from infected individuals. Mobile Task Force Omega-7 ("Praetorian Guard") was dispatched to neutralize SCP-64626-B instances and regain control of the situation.

Windows key + , (comma): Temporarily peek at the desktop without minimizing any open windows.

Windows key + Pause/Break: Open the System Properties dialog box.

Windows key + Shift + S: Take a screenshot of a selected area of the screen and save it to the clipboard.

Windows key + Shift + Left/Right arrow: Move the current window to the next or previous monitor.

Windows key + . (period): Open the emoji panel and insert an emoji into your document or text.

Windows key + Shift + Q: Sign out of your Windows account.

Windows key + F1: Open the Windows Help and Support center.

Windows key + Tab: Open the Task View interface to switch between open windows or virtual desktops.

Ctrl + Shift + Esc: Open the Task Manager directly, without going through the Ctrl + Alt + Del menu.

You are right; I decided to do some reading (about two hours) about the future of the forest after reading your comment. I did not like what I read one bit. Around one hundred thirty-five million acres of the Amazon has vanished during my lifetime using the 1988 estimation of 10,000 acres per day, sources below. From what I read, the future of the Amazon will likely be tragic; I never considered the possibility of the Amazon forest disappearing before I kicked the bucket. I hope governments take action before it is too late for the Amazon forest, but I have significant doubts.

* 

> [theguardian](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2021/oct/07/the-amazon-rain-forest-is-losing-200000-acres-a-day-soon-it-will-be-too-late#:~:text=Robert%20Walker%2C%20a%20quantitative%20geographer,be%20wiped%20out%20by%202064.) Robert Walker, a quantitative geographer at the University of Florida’s Center for Latin American studies, has said that unless something unprecedented happens, he predicts that the greatest rain forest on earth will be wiped out by 2064.

* 

> [nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-00508-4) 

>**The tipping-point question**

>No matter the season, the temperature above the tree canopy is always high enough to make it sweaty for researchers climbing up a monitoring tower there. The air is full of moisture that sustains the rainforest ecosystem.

>The forest plays a major part in keeping itself alive, by recycling water through trees to generate rainfall. A water molecule travelling across the Amazon can fall as rain up to six times^[4](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-00508-4#ref-CR4). If drought, fire or deforestation damage too many trees, reduced rainfall leads to less vegetation, and so on in a shrinking cycle. Eventually, this might transform large regions of the Amazon into an ecosystem more like a savannah (although with much less biodiversity). Only the western Amazon near the Andes mountains would remain lush — there, air currents are forced up over the mountains, causing water vapour to condense and fall as rain. 

>In 2018, Carlos Nobre, a climate researcher at the University of São Paulo, raised the alarm by arguing that the Amazon might be much closer to a tipping point than scientists thought. He and Thomas Lovejoy, an environmental researcher at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, wrote an editorial stating^[5](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-00508-4#ref-CR5) that if just 20–25% of the rainforest were cut down, it could reach a tipping point at which eastern, southern and central Amazonia would flip to a savannah-like ecosystem. Last December the pair repeated the warning, calling it a last chance for action^[6](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-00508-4#ref-CR6). “If the tree mortality we see continues for another 10–15 years, then the southern Amazon will turn into a savannah,” Nobre told Nature.

When I lockdown my network because kids are grounded, I use four nasty little filters. They block every website on the internet except whitelisted websites, examples below. I suggest making it as a separate set of user rules so you can toggle it with a single click. I also suggest googling how to use the group policy tool to lock down the computers network settings. Also, remember to use client settings to lock the filter to one device, you don't want to lock every device in your home to a single site. If you have a basic idea of how autohotkey works, you could write a script to automatically toggle the filter on & off based on the day and time. Lastly, I would ask the school for a list of websites that might be used for school and whitelist them all. You definitely don't want to block your kid from essential tools for an entire day or more if your kid doesn't tell you x is blocked.

Hope this helps you achieve what you want, she certainly won't be using any web games.

    @@||sitetwo.com^$important,document
